L1·N8949unmasked layer
This weak, diffuse neuron gives small positive activations on clause- or phrase-opening function/name words ("if", "where", "Full", "Great", "Tax" in multi-word titles), and is much more strongly *suppressed* by forum/site boilerplate tokens — the opening apostrophe in "Discussion in 'Forum Name'", "thread" in "showthread.php", and "Off" in "Comments Off" — so it mainly acts as a negative detector of message-board/template markup.

L3·N6147unmasked layer
This is a low-magnitude, weakly selective neuron that fires at sentence/segment boundary positions — the newline or first token right after a sentence-final period (e.g. "\n", " Bookmark", " In") — rather than on any coherent semantic category; the same boundary context can also drive it strongly negative, so its polarity is context-dependent noise around discourse breaks.

L10·N11373unmasked layer
Weak/noisy neuron (mostly negative range) in third-person narrative prose: it peaks on the word right after a pronoun subject or possessive in personal-anecdote storytelling (e.g. "he felt **a** bit shy", "he **went** ahead", "chew**ed** on", "both **her** parents"), while it is most strongly suppressed at named-character subject+verb spots in fiction ("Kerr **wondered**", "**Car**ole", "**Jen**").
